subproblem.title: A top-degree covector of ℝⁿ normalised on the standard basis has Euclidean norm 1 and spans Λⁿ(ℝⁿ)
subproblem.statement:
Let n ∈ ℕ, ℝⁿ = Euclid n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 (i ∈ Fin n) the standard basis, and e = (e₀, …, e_{n−1}). Let δ be an n-covector of ℝⁿ (δ ∈ Covector (Euclid n) n, a continuous alternating n-linear form) with δ(e) = 1. Then:
(a) covectorEuclideanNorm δ = 1. Here covectorEuclideanNorm β = (Σ over strictly increasing I : Fin n → Fin n of β(b_{I(0)}, …, b_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2}, with b = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ.
(b) Every n-covector α of ℝⁿ satisfies α = α(e)·δ, as continuous alternating maps with pointwise scalar multiplication.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (δ : Covector (Euclid n) n), δ (fun i => EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)) = 1 → covectorEuclideanNorm δ = 1 ∧ ∀ α : Covector (Euclid n) n, α = α (fun i => EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)) • δ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent proof. There |dy|² = dy(e)² = 1, because the identity is the only strictly increasing I : Fin n → Fin n, and λ = λ(e)·dy by AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det. Compare Simon, Ch. 6 §1, (1.1)–(1.2) (printed pp. 131–132): {dx^α : α ∈ I_{n,P}} is a basis of Λⁿ(ℝ^P) with coefficients ω(e_{i₁}, …, e_{iₙ}); for P = n the only multi-index is (1, …, n), so Λⁿ(ℝⁿ) = ℝ·dx¹∧⋯∧dxⁿ.
Notation: e = (e₀, …, e_{n−1}), e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ). Let δ be an n-covector of ℝⁿ with δ(e) = 1.
1. (The standard basis.) Let b := (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ).toBasis, a basis of ℝⁿ indexed by Fin n (Module.Basis (Fin n) ℝ (Euclid n)). For each i, b_i = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ i = e_i (OrthonormalBasis.coe_toBasis, EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply), so the family b equals e. Let det_b be the determinant alternating map of b (Module.Basis.det).
2. (Every top-degree covector is a multiple of det_b.) Let β be any n-covector of ℝⁿ and v : Fin n → ℝⁿ. The underlying alternating map β.toAlternatingMap is indexed by Fin n, the index type of b. So AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det gives β.toAlternatingMap = β(b)·det_b. Evaluating at v and using b = e (step 1): β(v) = β(e)·det_b(v).
3. (Proof of (b).) Step 2 with β = δ and the hypothesis δ(e) = 1 gives δ(v) = det_b(v) for all v. Step 2 with β = α gives α(v) = α(e)·det_b(v) = α(e)·δ(v) = (α(e)·δ)(v) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.smul_apply). As v is arbitrary, α = α(e)·δ by extensionality of continuous alternating maps (ContinuousAlternatingMap.ext).
4. (The only strictly increasing self-map of Fin n is the identity.) Let I : Fin n → Fin n be strictly monotone. Then I is injective (StrictMono.injective), hence surjective because Fin n is finite (Finite.injective_iff_surjective). So range I = univ = range id. Both I and id are strictly monotone on the well-ordered type Fin n, so equal ranges force I = id (StrictMono.range_inj_of_wellFoundedLT).
5. (Proof of (a).) By definition (unfold covectorEuclideanNorm, with P = n), covectorEuclideanNorm δ = √S, where S = Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin n} (if StrictMono I then δ(basisFun(I 0), …, basisFun(I(n−1)))² else 0). By step 4, the condition StrictMono I fails for every I ≠ id, so those summands are 0. Hence S equals the summand at I = id (Finset.sum_eq_single id; id ∈ Finset.univ). For I = id the condition holds (strictMono_id), and (basisFun(id i))_i = (e_i)_i (EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply), so this summand is δ(e)² = 1² = 1. Therefore S = 1 and covectorEuclideanNorm δ = √1 = 1 (Real.sqrt_one). ∎
The case n = 0 is included: Fin 0 → Fin 0 has the single element id, det_b is the constant 1, and every step goes through unchanged.

theorem Submission.cbr_ci_pw_td_top_covector_spans : ∀ (n : ℕ) (δ : Covector (Euclid n) n), δ (fun i => EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)) = 1 → covectorEuclideanNorm δ = 1 ∧ ∀ α : Covector (Euclid n) n, α = α (fun i => EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)) • δ := by
  intro n δ hδ
  classical
  let b : Module.Basis (Fin n) ℝ (Euclid n) := (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ).toBasis
  have hbe : (⇑b : Fin n → Euclid n) = fun i => EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ) := by
    funext i; simp [b]
  have key : ∀ (β : Covector (Euclid n) n) (v : Fin n → Euclid n),
      β v = β (fun i => EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)) * b.det v := by
    intro β v
    have := congrArg (fun f => f v) (AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det b β.toAlternatingMap)
    simpa [hbe] using this
  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
  · have hmono : ∀ I : Fin n → Fin n, StrictMono I → I = id := by
      intro I hI
      have hsurj : Surjective I := Finite.injective_iff_surjective.1 hI.injective
      exact (hI.range_inj_of_wellFoundedLT strictMono_id).1 (by rw [hsurj.range_eq, range_id])
    have he : (fun i => EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ (id i)) = fun i => EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ) := by
      funext i; simp
    unfold covectorEuclideanNorm
    rw [Finset.sum_eq_single (id : Fin n → Fin n)]
    · simp only [strictMono_id, ↓reduceIte, he, hδ, one_pow, Real.sqrt_one]
    · intro I _ hI
      have hI' : ¬ StrictMono I := fun h => hI (hmono I h)
      simp only [hI', ↓reduceIte]
    · intro h; exact absurd (Finset.mem_univ _) h
  · intro α
    ext v
    rw [ContinuousAlternatingMap.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, key α v, key δ v, hδ, one_mul]
proof_key_steps: b := (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ).toBasis is a Module.Basis indexed by Fin n, and the family b equals e (EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply).
AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det applied to β.toAlternatingMap gives β(v) = β(e)·det_b(v) for every top-degree covector β.
With δ(e) = 1 this gives δ = det_b, hence α(v) = α(e)·δ(v) for all v, and α = α(e)·δ by ContinuousAlternatingMap.ext.
A strictly monotone I : Fin n → Fin n is injective, hence surjective, so range I = range id and I = id (StrictMono.range_inj_of_wellFoundedLT).
The sum defining covectorEuclideanNorm δ reduces to the I = id term (Finset.sum_eq_single), which is δ(e)² = 1, so covectorEuclideanNorm δ = √1 = 1.
